best_for: PC and Mac gamers who buy most of their games on Steam and want one launcher for their library, friends and automatic game updates.
description:
Steam is the game store and launcher from Valve Corporation, the company that also builds the Steam Deck handheld and the Valve Index VR headset. Game makers use its Steamworks tools and services to sell and run their games on Steam.

Beyond buying games, you can keep a wishlist, work through a discovery queue of suggestions, read player reviews and earn achievements. Each game has a hub with discussions, player uploads and news. Early Access lets you play games while they are still being made. You can join groups or form clans, trade items on the Community Market, and manage your account from the Steam app on iOS or Android. The store takes more than 100 payment methods in over 35 currencies.

points.title: The client is free, the games are not
points.text: Downloading Steam costs nothing. Buying, playing and chatting go through a Steam account, and the store lists close to 30,000 games, from big studio titles to small indie ones.

points.title: Refunds follow a two-hour rule
points.text: Valve refunds most games when you ask within two weeks of purchase and have played less than two hours. DLC, in-game items in Valve games and subscriptions have their own rules, and video content is generally not refundable.

points.title: More than a store
points.text: Steam Chat, friends and groups, game broadcasting and the Workshop, which hosts mods and items for nearly 1,000 games. The client comes in 28 languages and supports game controllers.

points.title: Older Macs get cut off
points.text: Valve stopped supporting macOS 11 on October 15, 2025, and says future builds need macOS 12 or later. The reason given is the built-in copy of Google Chrome that core parts of Steam rely on, which stops working on old macOS versions.

points.title: Windows 10 or later
points.text: The Windows download is a 32-bit setup that installs for all users and needs Windows 10 or later.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not marked verified
points.text: Valve's about page offers downloads for Windows, macOS, SteamOS and ChromeOS, and does not name other Linux systems. The Flatpak listed here names Valve as developer, but Flathub does not mark it as verified, and it is x64 only.

points.title: Only the current client is listed
points.text: Each platform lists only the current release, so an older client build needs another source.
